brief: Goldman's Daan Struyven raised Brent and WTI forecasts by $5, to $85 and $80 for December 2026 and $80 and $75 for 2027, on a new assumption that Mideast shipping disruptions run into 2027. He calls the upgrade modest for two reasons. First, OECD commercial inventories, the stock category most predictive of Brent, have barely drawn: only 26mb of the 543mb global visible draw since the war, leaving Goldman's counter 119mb above its July balance estimate and its $79 fair value $18 below a $97 market. Second, Gulf supply keeps adapting, through dark flows, 3.8mb/d of new pipeline capacity by end-2027 and eventual spare capacity, returning to pre-war levels by 2027H2. Price-sensitive Chinese imports, down about 30% year over year, cap upside further, and Goldman puts fair value $10-15 higher had China held imports stable. Risks stay tilted upside: Brent above $120 in 2027 if Gulf output runs 4mb/d below pre-war, into the $60s if it runs 1mb/d above. Goldman still recommends hedging through deferred Mar27-Dec27 European diesel timespreads and long global natural gas and refined products.
